Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: The NIS is interfaced with multiple government systems providing online authentication of person identity and data. Government agencies query the NIS for authentication. The system supports real-time online authentication for services including electoral system, SOBERS, payroll and transport. A new fully digital authentication system is planned for the Digital ID rollout.
revision_notes: Confirmed. World Bank ID4D diagnostic (fetched) verifies NIS-based real-time online authentication interfaced with electoral, SOBERS, payroll and transport systems. 2026 government budget reporting confirms a broader Digital ID/e-authentication platform (evolved from the Electronic Identification System PPP) is under active development, alongside continued operation of the existing NIS authentication function. Score of 2 (Yes) upheld.
revised_comments: Botswana's National Identity System (NIS) is interfaced with multiple government platforms, including the electoral register, the Social Benefits Registration System (SOBERS), payroll and the transport registry, enabling real-time online authentication of citizens' identity and biographic data. A broader Digital ID and e-authentication platform, incorporating a smart Omang card, mobile app and e-wallet, is under active development as part of the government's Digital Ecosystem Model Project, with phased rollout targeted from 2025.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: Bank of Botswana banking regulations explicitly require Omang for KYC/customer identification. Financial institutions must verify identity using Omang for citizens. SIM card KYC requires Omang. The new Digital ID system explicitly aims to support electronic KYC (eKYC) with digital signatures and automated data exchange.
revision_notes: Confirmed via direct fetch. Regulation 5(1)(a) of the Bank of Botswana's Banking Act Regulations requires banks to obtain an Omang identity card for customer identification of citizens aged 16+ (or a passport for foreign nationals); the Financial Intelligence Regulations 2022 reinforce identity verification requirements for customer due diligence across accountable institutions. Score of 2 (Yes) upheld.
revised_comments: Botswana's Banking Act Regulations (Regulation 5) require banks to verify customers' identity using the Omang national identity card for citizens aged 16 and above, or a passport for foreign nationals, before establishing a business relationship. The Financial Intelligence Regulations 2022 reinforce these customer due diligence requirements across accountable institutions. Electronic/digital KYC verification against Omang records underpins customer onboarding in the banking and mobile-money sectors.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Botswana established a full organic link between birth registration, national registration (Omang), and death registration through a single unique identifier in 2003. The NIS is updated in real time when deaths are registered. UNICEF describes the two systems (CRVS and NIS) as 'operating efficiently and mutually interoperable'.
revision_notes: Confirmed via direct fetch of the World Bank ID4D diagnostic, which documents an organic link between birth registration, the National Identification System and death registration through a single unique identifier, with real-time NIS updates on death registration and interoperability with civil registration. UNICEF's evaluation similarly describes the CRVS and NIS as mutually interoperable. Score of 3 (Full integration) upheld.
revised_comments: Botswana's civil registration system and National Identification System (NIS) share a single unique identifier assigned at birth, later used for the Omang card issued at age 16. Death registrations trigger real-time updates to the NIS, and the Department of Civil and National Registration administers both systems jointly, giving Botswana one of the more fully integrated CRVS-ID architectures in the region.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The Omang card is designated as prima facie proof of identity under the National Registration Act. It serves as the primary document for accessing public services, voter registration, passport application, driving license, and other legal purposes.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The ID4D diagnostic and the National Registration Act (as summarised by the Botswana Embassy) describe the Omang as prima facie proof of identity, required for accessing public services, voter registration, passports, driving licences and other legal transactions. Score of 2 (Yes) upheld.
revised_comments: The National Registration Act designates the Omang card as prima facie proof of an individual's identity, and it is required for accessing public services, voter registration, passport applications, driving licences and other legal transactions.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: The National Registration Act CAP 01:02 provides the legal basis for compulsory national registration. The Births and Deaths Registration Act covers CRVS. The Electronic Transactions Act governs digital signatures. These create a comprehensive legal framework for the identity system.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The National Registration Act (CAP 01:02) establishes compulsory national registration and the Omang system; the Births and Deaths Registration Act covers CRVS; the Electronic Transactions Act (noted in the ID4D diagnostic as recently enacted) governs digital signatures and electronic records. Together these form the legal basis for the identity system. Score of 2 (Yes) upheld.
revised_comments: The National Registration Act (CAP 01:02) provides the legal basis for compulsory national registration and issuance of the Omang card, complemented by the Births and Deaths Registration Act for civil registration and the Electronic Transactions Act, which governs digital signatures and electronic records relevant to identity data.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: The DCNR is under the Ministry of Labour and Home Affairs (MLHA), not the Ministry of Finance. However, the Ministry of Finance provides general PFM oversight through budget approvals and the Public Finance Management framework. Annual ID system budgets are allocated through parliament. The MLHA has its own budget approved by parliament including P105 million for Omang card production in 2026/27.
revision_notes: Confirmed and refreshed. The Department of Civil and National Registration sits under the Ministry of Labour and Home Affairs (MLHA), not the Ministry of Finance, but MLHA's budget (including P105 million for Omang production and P42 million for Biometric Omang computerisation in 2026/27) is approved through parliament under standard public finance management oversight. No dedicated Ministry of Finance line-management of the ID system was found. Score of 2 (Partial oversight) upheld.
revised_comments: The Department of Civil and National Registration operates under the Ministry of Labour and Home Affairs, which holds primary responsibility for the ID system's budget and administration. The Ministry of Finance exercises general public financial management oversight through the annual budget approval process — the 2026/27 budget allocates P105 million for Omang card production and P42 million for the Biometric Omang computerisation project — but does not directly manage or finance the system.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: Botswana collects fingerprints (two thumbprints) and facial photo at enrollment. AFIS (Automated Fingerprint Identification System) is used for deduplication. First country in SADC to introduce AFIS. The upcoming system will be a multi-biometric platform.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The ID4D diagnostic and the APC review both confirm Omang enrolment captures fingerprints (used in the AFIS de-duplication system, in place since 1988 — the first in SADC) and a facial portrait image; no iris capture is used. This matches the 'Facial/Iris' biometric modality band given facial capture is confirmed. Score of 3 upheld.
revised_comments: Botswana collects fingerprints and a facial portrait photograph at Omang enrolment. The Automated Fingerprint Identification System (AFIS), in place since 1988, performs biometric de-duplication and was the first such system introduced in the SADC region. National ICT policy documents note plans to upgrade to a multi-biometric, next-generation platform, but iris capture is not currently used.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: The National Identity Management System (NIS) is linked with the electoral system, Social Benefit Registration System (SOBERS), government payroll, and transport system. Real-time updates occur when death registration events happen. The CRVS and NIS are mutually interoperable.
revision_notes: Confirmed via direct fetch of the ID4D diagnostic, which documents NIS interoperability with the Births and Deaths Registration System and describes system interfaces enabling data authentication across government agencies (electoral roll, SOBERS, payroll, transport). Score of 2 (Yes) upheld.
revised_comments: Botswana's National Identification System is interfaced with the Births and Deaths Registration System, the electoral register, the Social Benefits Registration System (SOBERS), government payroll and the transport registry, allowing cross-agency identity data authentication. A planned Population Register/People Hub project aims to further extend interoperability by linking the NIS with the Immigration and Citizenship System.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: Bank of Botswana Banking Regulations require banks to demand Omang from citizens for opening accounts and conducting transactions. Regulation 5(1)(a) states banks 'shall require its personal customers...to produce...Omang identity card for a citizen of Botswana above the age of sixteen'. This is a mandatory requirement under law.
revision_notes: Confirmed via direct fetch. Regulation 5(1)(a) of the Banking Act Regulations explicitly requires banks to obtain an Omang identity card from citizen customers above age 16 (or a passport for foreign nationals) before establishing business relations or conducting transactions. Score of 3 (Mandatory) upheld; exact enactment date of this specific regulation could not be independently confirmed beyond the original citation.
revised_comments: Bank of Botswana Banking Act Regulations require banks to obtain a customer's Omang identity card (for citizens aged 16 and above) or passport (for foreign nationals) before establishing a business relationship or conducting transactions, making the credential mandatory for accessing banking and financial services.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: First-time issuance of the Omang card is free. Renewal costs BWP5 (approximately US$0.37). Birth registration is also free. Late registration fees were waived from 2014 onwards for vulnerable populations. Only replacement for lost/stolen cards attracts a significant fee (BWP110/~US$8).
revision_notes: Confirmed and refreshed via the Government of Botswana civil registration fee schedule. First-time issuance of the Omang (registered within 30 days of turning 16) is free of charge. A fee of BWP5 applies to renewals, change-of-surname and damaged-card replacements, and BWP110 for lost/stolen cards; late registration attracts a fine of up to BWP500. Score of 2 (Yes, free of charge for first issuance) upheld.
revised_comments: First-time issuance of the Omang card, when registered within 30 days of an individual turning 16 or acquiring citizenship, is free of charge. Renewals, changes of surname and damaged-card replacements cost BWP5, while a lost or stolen card replacement costs BWP110; late registration attracts a fine of up to BWP500.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: Botswana and Namibia reached a bilateral agreement in February 2023 allowing citizens to use national ID cards for cross-border business and tourism travel (up to 30 days per stay, 90 days per year). A bilateral agreement with Zambia for smart national ID cross-border travel was announced in February 2026. Botswana is part of the SADC regional DPI/eKYC initiative across 16 countries. Cross-border recognition is partial/bilateral, not formally interoperable at the full SADC level.
revision_notes: Confirmed and refreshed. Since 2019/2023, Botswana and Namibia have permitted citizens to use national ID cards for cross-border travel of up to 90 days per year under the SADC Facilitation of Movement of Persons Protocol, with over 20,000 travellers using this route between 2023 and 2025. In February-March 2026, Botswana and Zambia reached a tentative agreement to extend ID-card-only travel to the Kazungula Bridge crossing. These remain bilateral arrangements rather than a formally interoperable regional (full-SADC) framework, so 'recognised in some regional contexts' remains the accurate score. Score of 2 upheld.
revised_comments: Botswana's national identity card (Omang) is recognised as a valid travel document under bilateral arrangements with neighbouring SADC states. Citizens of Botswana and Namibia have been able to cross their shared border using ID cards instead of passports since 2019/2023, for stays of up to 90 days per year, with over 20,000 such crossings recorded between 2023 and 2025. In early 2026, Botswana and Zambia reached a tentative agreement to extend ID-only travel to the Kazungula Bridge crossing. Recognition remains bilateral rather than part of a fully interoperable SADC-wide framework.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: National Registration Act requires enrollment within 30 days of turning 16 years old. Citizens must obtain Omang at age 16. This age threshold (16) falls in the 10-17 years range. The unique ID number given at birth is the same number used for the Omang card at age 16.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The National Registration Act and Government of Botswana registration guidance both require enrolment within 30 days of turning 16, placing the eligibility age within the 10-17 band. Score of 2 upheld.
revised_comments: Under the National Registration Act, citizens become eligible, and are required, to register for the Omang card within 30 days of turning 16 years of age (or acquiring Botswana citizenship), placing enrolment eligibility within the 10-17 age band. A unique identification number is assigned at birth and carried through to the Omang issued at 16.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: National Registration Act CAP 01:02 makes national registration compulsory for every citizen of Botswana within 30 days of turning 16 or acquiring citizenship. Failure to register within the prescribed period attracts a fine. Registration is mandatory for all eligible citizens.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The National Registration Act (CAP 01:02) makes registration compulsory for every citizen within 30 days of turning 16 or acquiring citizenship, with fines for late registration. Score of 3 upheld.
revised_comments: Registration for the Omang card is compulsory for all Botswana citizens under the National Registration Act, which requires enrolment within 30 days of turning 16 or acquiring citizenship. Late registration is subject to a fine of up to BWP500.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: The Ministry of Health adopted Omang as the unique identifier for all citizens seeking public health services. Non-citizens use passport numbers. This serves as the universal patient identifier across the public health sector. The Omang number is the primary key for patient data linkages in the public health information system.
revision_notes: Confirmed. WHO's Global Observatory on Digital Health country profile and the ID4D diagnostic both describe Omang as the unique identifier used by the Ministry of Health for citizens accessing public health services, functioning as the universal patient identifier in the public health information system. Score of 3 upheld.
revised_comments: The Ministry of Health uses the Omang number as the unique patient identifier for citizens accessing public healthcare services, underpinning patient data linkage across the public health information system; non-citizens are identified by passport number.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Omang is for Botswana citizens only. Non-citizens are registered in a separate Immigration and Citizenship System (ICS) — permanent residents, work permit holders, and refugees have separate registration. A project is ongoing to link NIS and ICS for a comprehensive Population Register. Some non-nationals (with permanent residence) have access to a form of registration but not the Omang card itself.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The Omang itself is restricted to citizens, but non-nationals with permanent residence, work permits or refugee status are captured in the separate Immigration and Citizenship System (ICS), which the government is working to integrate with the NIS into a single Population Register. This partial eligibility for some non-national categories supports a score of 2 (Some).
revised_comments: The Omang card is issued only to Botswana citizens. Non-nationals — including permanent residents, work-permit holders and refugees — are instead registered separately in the Immigration and Citizenship System, which the government is working to integrate with the National Identification System into a unified Population Register.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: The World Bank ID4D Country Diagnostic (2018) constitutes a formal independent security and quality review of Botswana's identity management system. The Omang card has first and second-level security features (visual and machine-readable). AFIS ensures uniqueness. Government formally cites 'data security and integrity management' as a component of the NIS. No evidence of a separate external cybersecurity audit process.
revision_notes: Original score of 2 (Yes) rested on treating the World Bank ID4D diagnostic itself as a 'security review' — but that diagnostic is a policy/institutional assessment, not a security audit, penetration test, or vulnerability assessment of the ID system, and the original comment itself concedes 'no evidence of a separate external cybersecurity audit process.' Direct reading of the diagnostic shows NIS data is not stored in encrypted form and there is no evidence of proactive breach monitoring. Botswana's National Cybersecurity Strategy (2021) confirms that, as of its drafting, critical national information infrastructure had not been formally identified and no cybersecurity audit regime was yet in place; conducting a 'Cyber Security Audit on the management, operation and infrastructure' is listed as a planned future action rather than a completed activity. No subsequent evidence was found of a dedicated, regular security audit, penetration test, or vulnerability assessment specific to the Omang/NIS system. Revised down to 1 (No). Flagged for human review since this reverses the original score and rests on absence-of-evidence reasoning rather than a direct disconfirming source.
revised_comments: No evidence of dedicated, regular security audits, penetration testing or vulnerability assessments of Botswana's national identity (Omang/NIS) system has been identified. National records show that key data is not stored in encrypted form, and the 2021 National Cybersecurity Strategy indicates that critical information infrastructure had not yet been formally identified for audit purposes, with cybersecurity audits framed as a planned future action rather than an established practice.
